<reason>A more convincingly separated meaningful transparency from the proposition’s specific navigation deadline. It directly answered pressure with enforceable honest totals, prominent suitability restrictions, and obligation-free review. B’s bright-line defense was relevant, but repeatedly treated that alternative as voluntary drip pricing and dismissed staged presentation’s attention costs without resolving them. A therefore left the mandate’s additional restriction insufficiently justified.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A neutralized B’s central price-surprise example by showing that enforceable upfront totals already prevent it. A then exposed B’s false choice between costless earlier disclosure and manipulative placement: comparison and confirmation can legitimately demand different presentations, even when platforms already possess the information.</best_rebuttal>
